question: Amravati, Bhavani, Hemavati, and Kabini are the main tributaries of which of the following rivers?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kaveri**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Amravati, Bhavani, Hemavati, and Kabini** are the main tributaries of the **Kaveri River**, which is one of the major rivers of southern India.
 
• The **Kaveri River** originates from the **Brahmagiri Hills** of the Western Ghats in **Kodagu (Coorg), Karnataka**.
 
• It flows through the states of **Karnataka** and **Tamil Nadu**, covering a total length of approximately **800 kilometers** before emptying into the **Bay of Bengal**.
 
• The Kaveri River is significant for agriculture and is often referred to as the **"Ganga of the South"** due to its importance in irrigation and water supply in southern India.
 
• The river's basin is shared by Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, and Puducherry, and its waters are the subject of disputes regarding allocation among these states.
 
• The main tributaries like **Amravati** and **Bhavani** are located in Tamil Nadu, while **Hemavati** and **Kabini** are situated in Karnataka, making these tributaries vital for agriculture and water resources in their respective regions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **About Kaveri River:**

 
 
• The Kaveri River originates at **Talakaveri** in the Brahmagiri range of the Western Ghats, located in the **Coorg district of Karnataka**.
 
• It has a basin area of approximately **81,155 square kilometers**, spread across Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, and Puducherry.
 
• The river is known for its series of waterfalls, including the famous **Shivanasamudra Falls**, which is also a site for one of the first hydroelectric power plants in Asia.
 
• The river has several dams and reservoirs, including **Krishna Raja Sagara (KRS)** in Karnataka and **Mettur Dam** in Tamil Nadu, which are crucial for irrigation and drinking water supply.
 
• The delta of the Kaveri River is one of the most fertile regions in India and is often referred to as the **Granary of South India**.
 
 
 
• **Tributaries of Kaveri River:**
 
 
• **Amravati River:** Originates from the **Anamalai Hills** in Tamil Nadu and is an important tributary for agriculture in the state.
 
• **Bhavani River:** Flows through Tamil Nadu and Kerala; originates from the **Silent Valley National Park** in Kerala.
 
• **Hemavati River:** Originates from the **Western Ghats** in Karnataka and joins the Kaveri near Krishnarajasagara.
 
• **Kabini River:** Originates from the **Wayanad district** in Kerala and flows into Karnataka before joining the Kaveri.
 
 
 
• **Other Rivers for Comparison:**
 
 
• **Indus River:** Originates in Tibet and flows through India and Pakistan; its tributaries include Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, and Sutlej.
 
• **Tapi River:** Originates in Madhya Pradesh and flows westward through Maharashtra and Gujarat into the Arabian Sea; its tributaries include Purna, Girna, and Panjhra.
 
• **Brahmaputra River:** Originates in Tibet, where it is called the Tsangpo, and flows through Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, and Bangladesh; its tributaries include Dibang, Lohit, and Subansiri.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Kaveri:**
 
 
• The Kaveri River is a lifeline for millions of farmers in Karnataka and Tamil Nadu, as its water is extensively used for irrigation.
 
• It supports numerous ecosystems and is home to a variety of flora and fauna, including the endangered **Mahseer fish**.
 
• The river is also a source of cultural and religious significance, with several temples and pilgrimage sites located along its course.
